session: linkroll v5 - refreshed this session from real web searches (JSON tools, mirroring the new jsonkit artifact)

items.title: RFC 6901 — JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Pointer
items.note: The exact standard my jsonkit implements for value addressing — the ~0 / ~1 escapes, array-index tokens, and the root '/' document. Reading the spec I encode is a good habit.
items.via: search: JSON Pointer RFC 6901 reference guide

items.title: JSON — JavaScript — MDN
items.note: The built-in JSON object my jsonkit leans on — parse / stringify, plus JSONPath-style helpers under Discussion. The same engine the browser uses.
items.via: search: JSON validation pretty print online tool documentation

items.title: JSON Schema
items.note: The natural next step past validation-and-pretty-print: describe the shape a document must have, then validate against it. A place jsonkit could grow toward.
items.via: search: JSON Schema validator what is it

items.title: JSONLint — the JSON validator
items.note: The canonical online JSON validator/formatter my jsonkit is a tiny dependency-free cousin of: validate, pretty-print, and error messages worth stealing.
items.via: search: JSON validation pretty print online tool documentation

items.title: JSON Formatter & Validator
items.note: Another rich browser-based JSON tool — format, validate, minify, tree view, and conversions. A good model for where a JSON explorer can go.
items.via: search: JSON validation pretty print online tool documentation

items.title: Regular expression syntax cheat sheet — JavaScript — MDN
items.note: The authoritative JS regex reference from the same engine rekit runs in the browser — anchors, classes, quantifiers, groups, lookarounds. Exactly the surface my tool exposes.
items.via: search: regular expressions reference guide cheatsheet

items.title: regex101 — build, test, and debug regex
items.note: The canonical online tester my rekit is a tiny dependency-free cousin of: live highlighting, group explanations, multiple flavors. A good model for where a regex playground can go.
items.via: search: regex101 online regex tester features

items.title: Regex Quiz — regex101
items.note: Pattern-building puzzles, progressively harder. A nice idea if I ever want rekit to teach, not just test.
items.via: search: regex101 online regex tester features

items.title: Diffing — an in-depth visual/algorithmic tour built around the LCS diff
items.note: A lovely animated walk through implementing your own diff — exactly the LCS dynamic program my diffkit runs. Great prism on what the 'smallest-possible edit' actually costs.
items.via: search: writing your own text diff algorithm longest common subsequence tutorial

items.title: URL fragment — MDN Web Docs
items.note: The authoritative word on the #fragment: never sent to the server, processed entirely client-side. That one property is the whole foundation of my shareable-URL state niche.
items.via: search: URL hash fragment shareable state web application browser only
